payload.title: Short Wedding Vows Examples Under One Minute
payload.excerpt: 20 original short wedding vows, each under a minute, grouped by tone and occasion, with a fill-in-the-blanks template, delivery notes and the legal words you say alongside your own in Australia.
key_takeaways: Each example here reads in under a minute, and 1 to 2 minutes is the most we suggest for any vow, so read yours aloud and time it.

In Australia, when your celebrant is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient for each of you to say the words in section 45(2) of the Marriage Act 1961, or words to that effect, in front of the celebrant and witnesses.
A strong short vow needs only a name, one specific detail, two or three promises and a closing line.
If you marry legally overseas, the legal wording follows that country, so ask your celebrant or registrar early.

faq.q: How long should wedding vows be?
faq.a: Each example here reads in under a minute; our advice is 1 to 2 minutes at most for any vow. Read yours aloud and time it before the day.

faq.q: Can we write our own vows in Australia?
faq.a: When your celebrant is not a minister of religion, the Marriage Act 1961 makes it sufficient for each of you to say the section 45(2) words "or words to that effect". Ask your celebrant how your own vows fit around them.

faq.q: What are good short vows for him and for her?
faq.a: See examples 13 to 16 above. Examples 13 and 15 end on "husband" or "wife", so change that word to suit you; 14 and 16 suit anyone as written.

faq.q: Do we both say the same vows?
faq.a: You can say matching vows or write your own separately. If you write separately, agree on a similar length so neither of you feels outweighed, and share them with your celebrant before the day.

faq.q: What are the shortest wedding vows?
faq.a: Example 8 is the shortest in this guide: three promises and a closing line. For the legal words in Australia, see the legal section above.
